subject: [PATCH] mm/huge_memory: transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that pageout() cannot pass its refcount check due to PMD mapping holding an extra folio reference, which is dropped by mmu_gather only after TLB flush

Reviewer noted that writeback can run folio_mkclean() concurrently with another CPU holding a stale TLB entry reference, causing a silent lost write and missing PG_dirty

Reviewer noted that zap_huge_pmd() only handles one PMD under PTL and suggested flushing the TLB before calling folio_remove_rmap_pmd() to avoid stale TLB entries.
reviews.raw_body:
Right. pageout() cannot pass its refcount check while PMD mapping still
holds an extra folio ref, and mmu_gather drops that ref only after TLB
flush.

---

Yep. Writeback can run folio_mkclean() while that ref is still held,
though, and with rmap already gone it misses the PMD ...

---

zap_huge_pmd() only handles one PMD under PTL anyway ... how about just
flushing before folio_remove_rmap_pmd()?

---8<---
diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index afbb5974bd22..6fb34924ef66 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -2531,6 +2531,14 @@ bool zap_huge_pmd(struct mmu_gather *tlb, struct vm_area_struct *vma,
 	is_present = pmd_present(orig_pmd);
 	folio = normal_or_softleaf_folio_pmd(vma, addr, orig_pmd, is_present);
 	has_deposit = has_deposited_pgtable(vma, orig_pmd, folio);
+	/*
+	 * folio_mkclean() relies on the rmap to find writable mappings.
+	 * Flush stale TLB entries before removing it below.
+	 */
+	if (folio && is_present && !folio_test_anon(folio) &&
+	    pmd_dirty(orig_pmd))
+		tlb_flush_mmu_tlbonly(tlb);
+
 	if (folio)
 		zap_huge_pmd_folio(mm, vma, orig_pmd, folio, is_present);
 	if (has_deposit)
---

Cheers, Lance

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary:
Lance Yang noted that in the case of an initial shared write fault on non-DAX XFS, __handle_mm_fault() first tries to create a huge PMD, which fails and sends the fault to handle_pte_fault(). This path leaves an empty PMD without a PTE, calls do_pte_missing(), and eventually leads to finish_fault(), which sees FAULT_FLAG_WRITE and attempts to set a dirty+writable PMD with do_set_pmd(). Lance Yang pointed out that this can lead to silently lost writes if another CPU stores through a stale TLB entry while the folio is being cleaned, and suggested fixing this issue.

The reviewer pointed out that __handle_mm_fault() calls wp_huge_pmd() only when a write/unshare fault hits an existing read-only PMD THP, and that the initial shared write fault above runs page_mkwrite before do_set_pmd() installs the writable file PMD.

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where the pmd dirty bit is not being transferred to the folio when a huge page is zapped, leading to potential silent data loss in certain file systems like xfs. The problem arises because the TLB flush is deferred and can occur after the rmap has been dropped under the pmd lock, causing stale TLB entries to remain. To fix this, the patch aims to transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap, ensuring that data integrity is maintained even in the presence of concurrent writes.
